task.title: Put the bundled CLI on the user's PATH
task.description:
Agents drive Workbook from a terminal, so installing the desktop app has to put a `workbook` where a shell finds it. It must be the app's own build, so a user with no Homebrew has a CLI, and it must not overwrite a Homebrew install.

Decided 2026-09-15: a stable copy plus a marked profile block.

- On launch the app compares its bundled binary (`process.resourcesPath`) with the copy in a per-user directory it owns and copies when they differ: `~/Library/Application Support/Workbench/bin` on macOS, `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Workbench\bin` on Windows, `~/.local/share/workbench/bin` on Linux. The copy exists because the bundle moves when the app is dragged and is replaced on update.
- On macOS and Linux the app appends that directory to PATH in the user's shell profiles inside a marked block, the same pattern `scripts/setup-dev-env.sh` already uses, so later runs replace rather than duplicate. Appending means a Homebrew install earlier on PATH keeps winning; the two coexist. On Windows the app adds the directory to the user PATH in the registry.
- The sidebar's binary note already reports which binary the app is driving. It grows a line reporting which `workbook` a new terminal will resolve, so a Homebrew user who sees an older version in the terminal knows why.
- A new terminal is needed after the first run; the app says so once, not on every launch.

Depends on the move.
